bottleneck.description: AquaBeam/HYDROS Aquablation is the only robotic heat-free waterjet BPH therapy, but the broader BPH treatment market has many established alternatives (TURP, HoLEP, Rezum, UroLift, TULSA-PRO).

dependency.key_customers: Hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, urology practices treating BPH patients
dependency.key_suppliers: Contract manufacturers for AquaBeam/HYDROS console and single-use disposable handpieces; imaging (ultrasound) component suppliers

editorial.notes: While PROCEPT is the sole vendor of its specific Aquablation modality, BPH is a treatment continuum with abundant clinical substitutes: Boston Scientific's Rezum (water vapor), Teleflex's UroLift (implants), HoLEP laser enucleation, traditional TURP, and Profound Medical's TULSA-PRO. From a supply-chain bottleneck perspective, displacement of PROCEPT would have no downstream supply-chain consequence — urologists would route patients to alternative therapies. The 'first/only' framing is therapeutic differentiation, not a structural bottleneck like ASML or 6920 JP. Therapy-area sole-source is not the same as supply-chain sole-source.
